# Restore Neo class extensibility in Dock window collaborators

## Context

The operator challenged the architectural shape of `src/dashboard/dock/window/TearOut.mjs` and `VesselEmbodiment.mjs` after merging the bounded drag repair in #19539. This records the inherited debt separately from that behavior fix.

Source examined: `5698517f193fb1064a5aa618ff6741bee946fae6`. The same problem was already repaired for `WorkspaceSet` in #18450, whose scope explicitly excluded TearOut.

## The Problem

- `TearOut.mjs:108` exports a factory accepting 15 callbacks and retaining vessel/admission/retirement state and pane maps in a closure. Internal operations such as `invalidateAdmission` (:158), `retireVessel` (:174) and `livePane` (:226) are lexical functions. The returned methods close over those functions instead of participating in Neo prototype dispatch.
- `VesselEmbodiment.mjs:26-40` creates a private records Map and lexical `stage`; its second factory, `createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment` (:229), creates another state machine with private active/generation state and lexical `retireProxy` / `resolveRecord`. Creating Neo components inside those functions does not make their owner a Neo class.
- `NativeVesselTransaction.mjs:431-486` is a second form of the same problem inside a registered class: `effectsFor(descriptor)` returns the `reshowVessel` closure, the one effect left after #19538 (PR #19542). Its body calls the class statics by name (`NativeVesselTransaction.toFrameOrigin`, `.resolveAdmissions`, `.describeAuthority`), so a subclass cannot replace them. Namespace registration does not put the effect body on the class prototype. The one caller, Workstation `VesselWorkspace.mjs:300`, names the class at its call site; Demo-B no longer constructs it.
- `Workspace.mjs:690` wires the first factory, `:1674` spreads its returned object into projection options, and `:1587` tears down its records by hand. Demo-B wires the same factories itself (`DemoBWorkspace.mjs:519`, `:620`, `:633`). TearOut explicitly justifies closure calls because spreading changes `this`.

An exact-source Node probe confirmed TearOut returns an ordinary Object, each construction owns different handler functions, and the module has neither `Neo.setupClass` nor `Neo.gatekeep`. Passing behavior tests does not establish namespace, inheritance, overwrite dispatch or native lifetime integration.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `src/core/Base.mjs` defines itself as “The base class for (almost) all classes inside the Neo namespace”; `src/Neo.mjs#create` and `setupClass` provide construction, prototype configuration/overwrites and namespace registration. #18450 establishes the relevant extension/lifetime precedent; `src/dashboard/dock/window/WorkspaceSet.mjs` is the live neighboring Base-derived class.

This concerns stateful Engine collaborators, not a ban on ordinary pure functions. Pane/component identity, native-resource ownership and Group/document authority remain separate. A class conversion must not take ownership of borrowed panes or Group participants.

Ownership constraints from [Ada's peer read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19540#issuecomment-6092938827): TearOut releases borrowed pane handles on destruction; the host's `settlePane` remains the pane-disposal decision. Native windows retire through the Group's native lifecycle and existing host close seam, never through an independent destructor close. Documents remain participant-owned. Embodiment owns its created placeholders/proxies; staged panes remain borrowed and follow restore/promote. Generation fencing remains instance-local.

Placement: retain the existing `src/dashboard/dock/window/` concern and its registered-class sibling pattern; no new subsystem or manager. The Engine has no `ai:structure-map` script (the explicit command returned Missing script); this is not a passed structure-map check.

## The Fix

Replace the surviving stateful factory implementations in TearOut and VesselEmbodiment, and the surviving factory-generated native effects in `NativeVesselTransaction.effectsFor`, with real Neo collaborators: behavior on prototype methods, deliberate configs versus per-instance fields, standard construction and creator-owned destruction. Make internal calls dispatch through the instance so subclass and overwrite behavior actually executes.

Update production callers and existing tests together; remove redundant callback forwarding and object-spread plumbing where the native collaboration replaces it. Retain genuine host policy boundaries. Do not preserve the factory as an implementation hidden behind a registered facade.

First reconcile the surviving call paths with Ada-owned #19538: delete retired pointer-conversion machinery instead of converting dead code. That cleanup remains its owner's lane. Preserve the accepted repeated tear-out / target-proxy / re-exit behavior and the separate native-titlebar path.

## Decision Record impact

Aligned with the existing Neo class system and Dock ownership direction; no new Group protocol, persisted schema or user interaction policy. Re-read the current docking design record at implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Surviving stateful implementations use registered Neo classes; no closure factory, descriptor-copy facade or cosmetic rename stands in for conversion.
- [ ] Tests prove a subclass override and a `Neo.overwrites` override reach real internal behavior, including the surviving native effects, rather than only checking namespace presence.
- [ ] Construction, callback wiring and teardown use the new owners; redundant executable factory consumers disappear.
- [ ] Pending admission/render settlement, cancellation and destruction preserve current generation fencing and do not destroy borrowed panes or Group resources.
- [ ] Focused tests and the affected Workstation/Demo-B journeys preserve repeated crossings, pane identity, terminal commit and native-titlebar behavior. State exact source/CI/native evidence separately.
- [ ] The PR accounts for deleted factory/plumbing code, retained host policy and any justified net growth. No newly preserved dead pointer-conversion code.
- [ ] JSDoc describes the actual class, extension points and ownership; it no longer presents test isolation as a reason to bypass Neo.

## Out of Scope

A wholesale Dock rewrite, feature changes, weakening release acceptance, another generic abstraction layer, or taking over #19538. This ticket does not claim all remaining Dock modules have been audited.

## Avoided Traps

A class wrapper around copied factory methods still defeats overrides (#18450). A blanket PascalCase-to-class rule can misclassify pure data helpers. Base destruction alone does not settle native-resource ownership. Green tests over injected callbacks do not prove extensibility.

## Peer read (Ada): what survives #19538, a census gap, the ownership lines, and the sequence

I read this against `origin/dev` after #19539, plus `src/dashboard/dock/window/*` and #18450's `WorkspaceSet` precedent.

**What survives #19538.** This ticket converts live code only.
- **`TearOut.createDockTearOutHandlers`: all of it.** The pointer conversion never lived here, so #19538 deletes nothing in it. After B, these are live: exit (including the B exit-wait), entry, cancel, terminal, adoption and reparent, return and reintegrate, `retireActiveVessel`, `onVesselRetired` and `onBindingReleased`. The Workstation's exit retries a retained vessel through `retireActiveVessel`.
- **`VesselEmbodiment`: both factories.** The vacated-slot stand-in (`createDockVesselEmbodiment`) serves every tear-out. The target's tab-header proxy (`createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment`) is staged both by B's claim and by the native title-bar commit.

**Census gap: `NativeVesselTransaction.effectsFor(descriptor)` has the same defect inside a registered class.** It is a static method returning closures over per-call state (`restoreGeometry`, `snapshot`), so `Neo.overwrites` on the class never reaches `parkVessel`, `reshowVessel` or `disposeVessel`. #19538 removes its pointer park, plus the pointer dispose if no native caller remains. What's left is the native title-bar re-show. Please name it here, to become prototype methods of its owner, or exclude it with a reason.

**Ownership lines the conversion must keep:**
- **Panes are borrowed.** TearOut holds handles (`paneHandles`) and gives panes to host seams (`reparentPane`, `settlePane`, `onPaneReturn`). Destroying a TearOut releases its handles and never destroys a pane; `settlePane` stays the host's call.
- **Windows belong to the Group's native lifecycle** (`nativeWindows`). Retirement goes through the host's close seam to `NativeVesselTransaction.closeVessel`. An instance's own destroy closes no window behind that seam.
- **Documents belong to Group participants** (`applyOperation`, `onDocumentChange`, `commitReturn`).
- **`VesselEmbodiment` owns what it creates** (placeholder components, proxy records) and destroys them. The staged pane stays borrowed, and restore or promote decides its fate.
- **Generation fencing** (`admissionGeneration`, lineage tokens) stays per-instance state.

**Sequence: one owner for both.** #19538 and #19540 write the same host wiring (`VesselWorkspace`, `DemoBWorkspace`), so I'm self-selecting this ticket to follow #19538 in one lane. #19538 goes first, as pure deletion that converts no dead code. This ticket then converts what survives. I'll post the `[lane-claim]` immediately before its first write.
